summary: Master advanced data wrangling techniques with our comprehensive Python and R training. Enhance your skills and streamline your data analysis process today.
lede: Data wrangling uses Python and R to turn messy, multi-source data into clean, analysis-ready datasets. For data engineers, analytics managers, business intelligence specialists, research analysts and data scientists, the training covers importing and exploring data, handling missing values and outliers, joining and reshaping datasets, and building reusable cleaning and validation pipelines.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who work daily with messy, multi-source data and need to transform it into credible, analysis-ready evidence for decision-making.
modules: Foundations of Data Wrangling and Impact Assessment
Data Ingestion and Initial Exploration Techniques
Handling Missing Values, Outliers, and Duplicates
Data Merging, Joining, and Multi-Source Integration
Automated Cleaning Pipelines and Modular Function Design
Data Quality Validation and Automated Reporting
AI-Assisted Wrangling and Smart Data Cleaning
Performance Optimization for Large-Scale Data Wrangling
Capstone Project and Stakeholder Communication Strategy
Domain-Specific Wrangling: Finance, Healthcare, and IoT
Advanced Text and Categorical Wrangling for ML Readiness
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of Python (lists, dictionaries, functions) and R (data frames, vectors, basic functions); familiarity with Jupyter Notebook or RStudio; ability to run scripts and install packages. No prior machine learning or advanced statistics required. Technical Setup: Bring a laptop with Python 3.9+ and R 4.2+ pre-installed. We provide a setup guide 1 week before the course. All datasets and code are free/open-source; no commercial licenses required. Experience Level: Intermediate—ideal for professionals who already write basic scripts but need to master advanced wrangling for complex, multi-source datasets. Beginners should complete a Python/R fundamentals course first.
topics: Data science & machine learning in practice
